ESV.1: “Now these are the rules that you shall set before them.
ESV.2: When you buy a Hebrew slave,  he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free, for nothing.
ESV.3: If he comes in single, he shall go out single; if he comes in married, then his wife shall go out with him.
ESV.4: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out alone.
ESV.5: But if the slave plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
ESV.6: then his master shall bring him to God, and he shall bring him to the door or the doorpost. And his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall be his slave forever.
ESV.7: “When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she shall not go out as the male slaves do.
ESV.8: If she does not please her master, who has designated her  for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has broken faith with her.
ESV.9: If he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her as with a daughter.
ESV.10: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
ESV.11: And if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out for nothing, without payment of money.
ESV.12: “Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death.
ESV.13: But if he did not lie in wait for him, but God let him fall into his hand, then I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.
ESV.14: But if a man willfully attacks another to kill him by cunning, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.
ESV.15: “Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.
ESV.16: “Whoever steals a man and sells him, and anyone found in possession of him, shall be put to death.
ESV.17: “Whoever curses  his father or his mother shall be put to death.
ESV.18: “When men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist and the man does not die but takes to his bed,
ESV.19: then if the man rises again and walks outdoors with his staff, he who struck him shall be clear; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall have him thoroughly healed.
ESV.20: “When a man strikes his slave, male or female, with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, he shall be avenged.
ESV.21: But if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be avenged, for the slave is his money.
ESV.22: “When men strive together and hit a pregnant woman, so that her children come out, but there is no harm, the one who hit her shall surely be fined, as the woman's husband shall impose on him, and he shall pay as the judges determine.
ESV.23: But if there is harm,  then you shall pay life for life,
ESV.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
ESV.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
ESV.26: “When a man strikes the eye of his slave, male or female, and destroys it, he shall let the slave go free because of his eye.
ESV.27: If he knocks out the tooth of his slave, male or female, he shall let the slave go free because of his tooth.
ESV.28: “When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox shall not be liable.
ESV.29: But if the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has been warned but has not kept it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.
ESV.30: If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed on him.
ESV.31: If it gores a man's son or daughter, he shall be dealt with according to this same rule.
ESV.32: If the ox gores a slave, male or female, the owner shall give to their master thirty shekels  of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
ESV.33: “When a man opens a pit, or when a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
ESV.34: the owner of the pit shall make restoration. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead beast shall be his.
ESV.35: “When one man's ox butts another's, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and share its price, and the dead beast also they shall share.
ESV.36: Or if it is known that the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall repay ox for ox, and the dead beast shall be his.

NASB.1: 'Now these are the ordinances which you are to set before them:
NASB.2: 'If you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve for six years; but on the seventh he shall go out as a free man without payment.
NASB.3: 'If he comes alone, he shall go out alone; if he is the husband of a wife, then his wife shall go out with him.
NASB.4: 'If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out alone.
NASB.5: 'But if the slave plainly says, 'I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not go out as a free man,'
NASB.6: then his master shall bring him to God, then he shall bring him to the door or the doorpost. And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl; and he shall serve him permanently.
NASB.7: 'If a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she is not to go free as the male slaves do.
NASB.8: 'If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He does not have authority to sell her to a foreign people because of his unfairness to her.
NASB.9: 'If he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the custom of daughters.
NASB.10: 'If he takes to himself another woman, he may not reduce her food, her clothing, or her conjugal rights.
NASB.11: 'If he will not do these three [things] for her, then she shall go out for nothing, without [payment of] money.
NASB.12: 'He who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.
NASB.13: 'But if he did not lie in wait [for him], but God let [him] fall into his hand, then I will appoint you a place to which he may flee.
NASB.14: 'If, however, a man acts presumptuously toward his neighbor, so as to kill him craftily, you are to take him [even] from My altar, that he may die.
NASB.15: 'He who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
NASB.16: 'He who kidnaps a man, whether he sells him or he is found in his possession, shall surely be put to death.
NASB.17: 'He who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
NASB.18: 'If men have a quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with [his] fist, and he does not die but remains in bed,
NASB.19: if he gets up and walks around outside on his staff, then he who struck him shall go unpunished; he shall only pay for his loss of time, and shall take care of him until he is completely healed.
NASB.20: 'If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod and he dies at his hand, he shall be punished.
NASB.21: 'If, however, he survives a day or two, no vengeance shall be taken; for he is his property.
NASB.22: 'If men struggle with each other and strike a woman with child so that she gives birth prematurely, yet there is no injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman's husband may demand of him, and he shall pay as the judges [decide].
NASB.23: 'But if there is [any further] injury, then you shall appoint [as a penalty] life for life,
NASB.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
NASB.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
NASB.26: 'If a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave, and destroys it, he shall let him go free on account of his eye.
NASB.27: 'And if he knocks out a tooth of his male or female slave, he shall let him go free on account of his tooth.
NASB.28: 'If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall surely be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall go unpunished.
NASB.29: 'If, however, an ox was previously in the habit of goring and its owner has been warned, yet he does not confine it and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.
NASB.30: 'If a ransom is demanded of him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is demanded of him.
NASB.31: 'Whether it gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
NASB.32: 'If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner shall give his [or her] master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
NASB.33: 'If a man opens a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it over, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
NASB.34: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he shall give money to its owner, and the dead [animal] shall become his.
NASB.35: 'If one man's ox hurts another's so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide its price equally; and also they shall divide the dead [ox].
NASB.36: 'Or [if] it is known that the ox was previously in the habit of goring, yet its owner has not confined it, he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead [animal] shall become his.

NKJV.1: “Now these are the judgments which you shall set before them:
NKJV.2: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years; and in the seventh he shall go out free and pay nothing.
NKJV.3: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself; if he comes in married, then his wife shall go out with him.
NKJV.4: If his master has given him a wife, and she has borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.
NKJV.5: But if the servant plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
NKJV.6: then his master shall bring him to the judges. He shall also bring him to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl; and he shall serve him forever.
NKJV.7: “And if a man sells his daughter to be a female slave, she shall not go out as the male slaves do.
NKJV.8: If she does not please her master, who has betrothed her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.
NKJV.9: And if he has betrothed her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the custom of daughters.
NKJV.10: If he takes another wife, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marriage rights.
NKJV.11: And if he does not do these three for her, then she shall go out free, without paying money.
NKJV.12: “He who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.13: However, if he did not lie in wait, but God delivered him into his hand, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
NKJV.14: “But if a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him by treachery, you shall take him from My altar, that he may die.
NKJV.15: “And he who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.16: “He who kidnaps a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.17: “And he who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.18: “If men contend with each other, and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to his bed,
NKJV.19: if he rises again and walks about outside with his staff, then he who struck him shall be acquitted. He shall only pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for him to be thoroughly healed.
NKJV.20: “And if a man beats his male or female servant with a rod, so that he dies under his hand, he shall surely be punished.
NKJV.21: Notwithstanding, if he remains alive a day or two, he shall not be punished; for he is his property.
NKJV.22: “If men fight, and hurt a woman with child, so that she gives birth prematurely, yet no harm follows, he shall surely be punished accordingly as the woman’s husband imposes on him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.
NKJV.23: But if any harm follows, then you shall give life for life,
NKJV.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
NKJV.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
NKJV.26: “If a man strikes the eye of his male or female servant, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for the sake of his eye.
NKJV.27: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male or female servant, he shall let him go free for the sake of his tooth.
NKJV.28: “If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, then the ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be acquitted.
NKJV.29: But if the ox tended to thrust with its horn in times past, and it has been made known to his owner, and he has not kept it confined, so that it has killed a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.
NKJV.30: If there is imposed on him a sum of money, then he shall pay to redeem his life, whatever is imposed on him.
NKJV.31: Whether it has gored a son or gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.
NKJV.32: If the ox gores a male or female servant, he shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
NKJV.33: “And if a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls in it,
NKJV.34: the owner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money to their owner, but the dead animal shall be his.
NKJV.35: “If one man’s ox hurts another’s, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide the money from it; and the dead ox they shall also divide.
NKJV.36: Or if it was known that the ox tended to thrust in time past, and its owner has not kept it confined, he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead animal shall be his own.

NLT.1: “These are the regulations you must present to Israel.
NLT.2: “If you buy a Hebrew slave, he may serve for no more than six years. Set him free in the seventh year, and he will owe you nothing for his freedom.
NLT.3: If he was single when he became your slave, he shall leave single. But if he was married before he became a slave, then his wife must be freed with him.
NLT.4: “If his master gave him a wife while he was a slave and they had sons or daughters, then only the man will be free in the seventh year, but his wife and children will still belong to his master.
NLT.5: But the slave may declare, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I don’t want to go free.’
NLT.6: If he does this, his master must present him before God. Then his master must take him to the door or doorpost and publicly pierce his ear with an awl. After that, the slave will serve his master for life.
NLT.7: “When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she will not be freed at the end of six years as the men are.
NLT.8: If she does not satisfy her owner, he must allow her to be bought back again. But he is not allowed to sell her to foreigners, since he is the one who broke the contract with her.
NLT.9: But if the slave’s owner arranges for her to marry his son, he may no longer treat her as a slave but as a daughter.
NLT.10: “If a man who has married a slave wife takes another wife for himself, he must not neglect the rights of the first wife to food, clothing, and sexual intimacy.
NLT.11: If he fails in any of these three obligations, she may leave as a free woman without making any payment.
NLT.12: “Anyone who assaults and kills another person must be put to death.
NLT.13: But if it was simply an accident permitted by God, I will appoint a place of refuge where the slayer can run for safety.
NLT.14: However, if someone deliberately kills another person, then the slayer must be dragged even from my altar and be put to death.
NLT.15: “Anyone who strikes father or mother must be put to death.
NLT.16: “Kidnappers must be put to death, whether they are caught in possession of their victims or have already sold them as slaves.
NLT.17: “Anyone who dishonors father or mother must be put to death.
NLT.18: “Now suppose two men quarrel, and one hits the other with a stone or fist, and the injured person does not die but is confined to bed.
NLT.19: If he is later able to walk outside again, even with a crutch, the assailant will not be punished but must compensate his victim for lost wages and provide for his full recovery.
NLT.20: “If a man beats his male or female slave with a club and the slave dies as a result, the owner must be punished.
NLT.21: But if the slave recovers within a day or two, then the owner shall not be punished, since the slave is his property.
NLT.22: “Now suppose two men are fighting, and in the process they accidentally strike a pregnant woman so she gives birth prematurely. If no further injury results, the man who struck the woman must pay the amount of compensation the woman’s husband demands and the judges approve.
NLT.23: But if there is further injury, the punishment must match the injury: a life for a life,
NLT.24: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,
NLT.25: a burn for a burn, a wound for a wound, a bruise for a bruise.
NLT.26: “If a man hits his male or female slave in the eye and the eye is blinded, he must let the slave go free to compensate for the eye.
NLT.27: And if a man knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free to compensate for the tooth.
NLT.28: “If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must be stoned, and its flesh may not be eaten. In such a case, however, the owner will not be held liable.
NLT.29: But suppose the ox had a reputation for goring, and the owner had been informed but failed to keep it under control. If the ox then kills someone, it must be stoned, and the owner must also be put to death.
NLT.30: However, the dead person’s relatives may accept payment to compensate for the loss of life. The owner of the ox may redeem his life by paying whatever is demanded.
NLT.31: “The same regulation applies if the ox gores a boy or a girl.
NLT.32: But if the ox gores a slave, either male or female, the animal’s owner must pay the slave’s owner thirty silver coins, and the ox must be stoned.
NLT.33: “Suppose someone digs or uncovers a pit and fails to cover it, and then an ox or a donkey falls into it.
NLT.34: The owner of the pit must pay full compensation to the owner of the animal, but then he gets to keep the dead animal.
NLT.35: “If someone’s ox injures a neighbor’s ox and the injured ox dies, then the two owners must sell the live ox and divide the price equally between them. They must also divide the dead animal.
NLT.36: But if the ox had a reputation for goring, yet its owner failed to keep it under control, he must pay full compensation — a live ox for the dead one — but he may keep the dead ox.

WEB.1: “Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.
WEB.2: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.
WEB.3: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.
WEB.4: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.
WEB.5: But if the servant shall plainly say, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go out free;’
WEB.6: then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever.
WEB.7: “If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants do.
WEB.8: If she doesn’t please her master, who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.
WEB.9: If he marries her to his son, he shall deal with her as a daughter.
WEB.10: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.
WEB.11: If he doesn’t do these three things for her, she may go free without paying any money.
WEB.12: “One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,
WEB.13: but not if it is unintentional, but God allows it to happen: then I will appoint you a place where he shall flee.
WEB.14: If a man schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to kill him, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.
WEB.15: “Anyone who attacks his father or his mother shall be surely put to death.
WEB.16: “Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
WEB.17: “Anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
WEB.18: “If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he doesn’t die, but is confined to bed;
WEB.19: if he rises again and walks around with his staff, then he who struck him shall be cleared: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.
WEB.20: “If a man strikes his servant or his maid with a rod, and he dies under his hand, he shall surely be punished.
WEB.21: Notwithstanding, if he gets up after a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his property.
WEB.22: “If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.
WEB.23: But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,
WEB.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
WEB.25: burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
WEB.26: “If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.
WEB.27: If he strikes out his male servant’s tooth, or his female servant’s tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.
WEB.28: “If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.
WEB.29: But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and it has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.
WEB.30: If a ransom is laid on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is laid on him.
WEB.31: Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.
WEB.32: If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels  of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.
WEB.33: “If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and doesn’t cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it,
WEB.34: the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
WEB.35: “If one man’s bull injures another’s, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and they shall also divide the dead animal.
WEB.36: Or if it is known that the bull was in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall surely pay bull for bull, and the dead animal shall be his own.

CSB17.1: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:
CSB17.2: “When you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years; then in the seventh he is to leave as a free man <sup>[1]</sup> without paying anything. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.3: If he arrives alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrives with <sup>[2]</sup> a wife, his wife is to leave with him.
CSB17.4: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children belong to her master, and the man must leave alone.
CSB17.5: “But if the slave declares, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I do not want to leave as a free man,’ <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.6: his master is to bring him to the judges <sup>[3]</sup> and then bring him to the door or doorpost. His master will pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve his master for life.
CSB17.7: “When a man sells his daughter as a concubine, <sup>[4]</sup> she is not to leave as the male slaves do. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: If she is displeasing to her master, who chose her for himself, then he must let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners because he has acted treacherously toward her.
CSB17.9: Or if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her according to the customary treatment of daughters.
CSB17.10: If he takes an additional wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of the first wife. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.11: And if he does not do these three things for her, she may leave free of charge, without any payment. <sup>[5]</sup>
CSB17.12: “Whoever strikes a person so that he dies must be put to death. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.13: But if he did not intend any harm, <sup>[6]</sup> and yet God allowed it to happen, I will appoint a place for you where he may flee. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.14: If a person schemes and willfully <sup>[7]</sup> acts against his neighbor to murder him, you must take him from my altar to be put to death. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.15: “Whoever strikes his father or his mother must be put to death.
CSB17.16: “Whoever kidnaps a person must be put to death, whether he sells him or the person is found in his possession. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.17: “Whoever curses his father or his mother must be put to death. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.18: “When men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or his fist, and the injured man does not die but is confined to bed,
CSB17.19: if he can later get up and walk around outside leaning on his staff, then the one who struck him will be exempt from punishment. Nevertheless, he must pay for his lost work time <sup>[8]</sup> and provide for his complete recovery.
CSB17.20: “When a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his abuse, <sup>[9]</sup> the owner must be punished. <sup>[10]</sup>
CSB17.21: However, if the slave can stand up after a day or two, the owner should not be punished <sup>[11]</sup> because he is his owner’s property. <sup>[12]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.22: “When men get in a fight and hit a pregnant woman so that her children are born prematurely but there is no injury, the one who hit her must be fined as the woman’s husband demands <sup>ⓖ</sup> from him, and he must pay according to judicial assessment.
CSB17.23: If there is an injury, then you must give life for life,
CSB17.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, <sup>ⓗ</sup> hand for hand, foot for foot,
CSB17.25: burn for burn, bruise for bruise, wound for wound.
CSB17.26: “When a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he must let the slave go free in compensation for his eye.
CSB17.27: If he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free in compensation for his tooth.
CSB17.28: “When an ox <sup>[13]</sup> gores a man or a woman to death, the ox must be stoned, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and its meat may not be eaten, but the ox’s owner is innocent.
CSB17.29: However, if the ox was in the habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and its owner must also be put to death.
CSB17.30: If instead a ransom <sup>ⓙ</sup> is demanded of him, he can pay a redemption price for his life in the full amount demanded from him.
CSB17.31: If it gores a son or a daughter, he is to be dealt with according to this same law.
CSB17.32: If the ox gores a male or female slave, he must give thirty shekels <sup>ⓚ</sup> of silver <sup>[14]</sup> to the slave’s master, and the ox must be stoned.
CSB17.33: “When a man uncovers a pit or digs a pit, and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
CSB17.34: the owner of the pit must give compensation; he must pay to its owner, but the dead animal will become his.
CSB17.35: “When a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live ox and divide its proceeds; they must also divide the dead animal.
CSB17.36: If, however, it is known that the ox was in the habit of goring, yet its owner has not restrained it, he must compensate fully, ox for ox; the dead animal will become his.

AMP.1: "Now these are the ordinances (laws) which you shall set before the Israelites:
AMP.2: "If you purchase a Hebrew servant [because of his debt or poverty], he shall serve six years, and in the seventh [year] he shall leave as a free man, paying nothing.
AMP.3: If he came [to you] alone, he shall leave alone; if he came married, then his wife shall leave with him.
AMP.4: If his master gives him a wife, and she gives birth to sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall leave [your service] alone.
AMP.5: But if the servant plainly says, 'I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not leave as a free man,'
AMP.6: then his master shall bring him to God [that is, to the judges who act in God's name], then he shall bring him to the door or doorpost. And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl (strong needle); and he shall serve him for life.
AMP.7: "If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go free [after six years] as male servants do.
AMP.8: If she does not please her master who has chosen her for himself [as a wife], he shall let her be redeemed [by her family]. He does not have the authority to sell her to a foreign people, because he has been unfair to her.
AMP.9: If her master chooses her [as a wife] for his son, he shall act toward her as if she were legally his daughter.
AMP.10: If her master marries another wife, he may not reduce her food, her clothing, or her privilege as a wife.
AMP.11: If he does not do these three things for her, then shall she leave free, without payment of money.
AMP.12: "Whoever strikes a man so that he dies must be put to death.
AMP.13: However, if he did not lie in wait [for him], but God allowed him to fall into his hand, then I will establish for you a place to which he may escape [for protection until duly tried].
AMP.14: But if a man acts intentionally against another and kills him by [design through] treachery, you are to take him from My altar [to which he may have fled for protection], so that he may be put to death.
AMP.15: "Whoever strikes his father or his mother must be put to death.
AMP.16: "Whoever kidnaps a man, whether he sells him or is found with him in his possession, must be put to death.
AMP.17: "Whoever curses his father or his mother or treats them contemptuously must be put to death.
AMP.18: "If men quarrel and one strikes another with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
AMP.19: if he gets up and walks around leaning on his cane, then the one who struck him shall be left [physically] unpunished; he must only pay for his loss of time [at work], and the costs [of treatment and recuperation] until he is thoroughly healed.
AMP.20: "If a man strikes his male or his female servant with a staff and the servant dies at his hand, he must be punished.
AMP.21: If, however, the servant survives for a day or two, the offender shall not be punished, for the [injured] servant is his own property.
AMP.22: "If men fight with each other and injure a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely [and the baby lives], yet there is no further injury, the one who hurt her must be punished with a fine [paid] to the woman's husband, as much as the judges decide.
AMP.23: But if there is any further injury, then you shall require [as a penalty] life for life,
AMP.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
AMP.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
AMP.26: "If a man hits the eye of his male servant or female servant and it is destroyed, he must let the servant go free because of [the loss of] the eye.
AMP.27: And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or female servant, he must let the servant go free because of [the loss of] the tooth.
AMP.28: "If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox must be stoned and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be cleared [of responsibility].
AMP.29: But if the ox has tried to gore on a previous occasion, and its owner has been warned, but has not kept it confined and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner shall be put to death as well.
AMP.30: If a ransom is demanded of him [in return for his life], then he shall give whatever is demanded for the redemption of his life.
AMP.31: If the ox has gored another's son or daughter, he shall be dealt with according to this same rule.
AMP.32: If the ox gores a male or a female servant, the owner shall give to the servant's master thirty shekels of silver [the purchase price for a slave], and the ox shall be stoned.
AMP.33: "If a man leaves a pit open, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
AMP.34: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he shall give money to the animal's owner, but the dead [animal] shall be his.
AMP.35: "If one man's ox injures another's so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide the proceeds equally; they shall also divide the dead ox [between them].
AMP.36: Or if it is known that the ox was previously in the habit of goring, and its owner has not kept it confined, he must make restitution of ox for ox, and the dead [animal] shall be his.

NRSVCE.14: But if someone willfully attacks and kills another by treachery, you shall take the killer from my altar for execution.
NRSVCE.15: Whoever strikes father or mother shall be put to death.
NRSVCE.16: Whoever kidnaps a person, whether that person has been sold or is still held in possession, shall be put to death.
NRSVCE.17: Whoever curses father or mother shall be put to death.
NRSVCE.18: When individuals quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or fist so that the injured party, though not dead, is confined to bed,
NRSVCE.19: but recovers and walks around outside with the help of a staff, then the assailant shall be free of liability, except to pay for the loss of time, and to arrange for full recovery.
NRSVCE.20: When a slaveowner strikes a male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies immediately, the owner shall be punished.
NRSVCE.21: But if the slave survives a day or two, there is no punishment; for the slave is the owner’s property.
NRSVCE.22: When people who are fighting injure a pregnant woman so that there is a miscarriage, and yet no further harm follows, the one responsible shall be fined what the woman’s husband demands, paying as much as the judges determine.
NRSVCE.23: If any harm follows, then you shall give life for life,
NRSVCE.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
NRSVCE.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
NRSVCE.26: When a slaveowner strikes the eye of a male or female slave, destroying it, the owner shall let the slave go, a free person, to compensate for the eye.
NRSVCE.27: If the owner knocks out a tooth of a male or female slave, the slave shall be let go, a free person, to compensate for the tooth.
NRSVCE.28: When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall not be liable.
NRSVCE.29: If the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has been warned but has not restrained it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.
NRSVCE.30: If a ransom is imposed on the owner, then the owner shall pay whatever is imposed for the redemption of the victim’s life.
NRSVCE.31: If it gores a boy or a girl, the owner shall be dealt with according to this same rule.
NRSVCE.32: If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner shall pay to the slaveowner thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
NRSVCE.33: If someone leaves a pit open, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
NRSVCE.34: the owner of the pit shall make restitution, giving money to its owner, but keeping the dead animal.
NRSVCE.35: If someone’s ox hurts the ox of another, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live ox and divide the price of it; and the dead animal they shall also divide.
NRSVCE.36: But if it was known that the ox was accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has not restrained it, the owner shall restore ox for ox, but keep the dead animal.

NET.1: “These are the decisions that you will set before them:
NET.2: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years, but in the seventh year he will go out free without paying anything.
NET.3: If he came in by himself he will go out by himself; if he had a wife when he came in, then his wife will go out with him.
NET.4: If his master gave him a wife, and she bore sons or daughters, the wife and the children will belong to her master, and he will go out by himself.
NET.5: But if the servant should declare, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
NET.6: then his master must bring him to the judges, and he will bring him to the door or the doorposts, and his master will pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
NET.7: “If a man sells his daughter as a female servant, she will not go out as the male servants do.
NET.8: If she does not please her master, who has designated her for himself, then he must let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has dealt deceitfully with her.
NET.9: If he designated her for his son, then he will deal with her according to the customary rights of daughters.
NET.10: If he takes another wife, he must not diminish the first one’s food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
NET.11: If he does not provide her with these three things, then she will go out free, without paying money.
NET.12: “Whoever strikes someone so that he dies must surely be put to death.
NET.13: But if he does not do it with premeditation, but it happens by accident, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
NET.14: But if a man willfully attacks his neighbor to kill him cunningly, you will take him even from my altar that he may die.
NET.15: “Whoever strikes his father or his mother must surely be put to death.
NET.16: “Whoever kidnaps someone and sells him, or is caught still holding him, must surely be put to death.
NET.17: “Whoever treats his father or his mother disgracefully must surely be put to death.
NET.18: “If men fight, and one strikes his neighbor with a stone or with his fist and he does not die, but must remain in bed,
NET.19: and then if he gets up and walks about outside on his staff, then the one who struck him is innocent, except he must pay for the injured person’s loss of time and see to it that he is fully healed.
NET.20: “If a man strikes his male servant or his female servant with a staff so that he or she dies as a result of the blow, he will surely be punished.
NET.21: However, if the injured servant survives one or two days, the owner will not be punished, for he has suffered the loss.
NET.22: “If men fight and hit a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no serious injury, he will surely be punished in accordance with what the woman’s husband demands of him, and he will pay what the court decides.
NET.23: But if there is serious injury, then you will give a life for a life,
NET.24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
NET.25: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
NET.26: “If a man strikes the eye of his male servant or his female servant so that he destroys it, he will let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
NET.27: If he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or his female servant, he will let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
NET.28: “If an ox gores a man or a woman so that either dies, then the ox must surely be stoned and its flesh must not be eaten, but the owner of the ox will be acquitted.
NET.29: But if the ox had the habit of goring, and its owner was warned, and he did not take the necessary precautions, and then it killed a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned and the man must be put to death.
NET.30: If a ransom is set for him, then he must pay the redemption for his life according to whatever amount was set for him.
NET.31: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, the owner will be dealt with according to this rule.
NET.32: If the ox gores a male servant or a female servant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver, and the ox must be stoned.
NET.33: “If a man opens a pit or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
NET.34: the owner of the pit must repay the loss. He must give money to its owner, and the dead animal will become his.
NET.35: If the ox of one man injures the ox of his neighbor so that it dies, then they will sell the live ox and divide its proceeds, and they will also divide the dead ox.
NET.36: Or if it is known that the ox had the habit of goring, and its owner did not take the necessary precautions, he must surely pay ox for ox, and the dead animal will become his.
